name: D3D_OcclusionQueryBeginEnd
note: an occlusion query's begin or end: its result address per tile, EVENT_WRITE_ZPD

name: D3D_PatchVertexFetches
note: a vertex shader's fetches remade from the declaration, swizzled, sorted and merged into mini-fetches

name: D3D_PatchedShaderCache
note: a vertex shader's patched copy for the device's state: cache hit, still in use, or patched again

name: D3D_RemapShaderExports
note: an output's export instructions given the input's register

name: D3D_ReplayCommandBuffer
note: a recorded command buffer's dirty state and replay

name: D3D_RingSubmit
note: a kicked segment into the primary ring: ring space waited for, an INDIRECT_BUFFER, CP_RB_WPTR (Any360: handed to the command processor directly)

name: D3D_SegmentClose
note: the kick's segment closed (its end packets, its submit) and the next one opened, or a new one from the allocator

name: D3D_SegmentEnd
note: a segment's end packets: INVALIDATE_STATE, the segment's end and count into the device's scratch (EVENT_WRITE_SHD)

name: D3D_SegmentSubmit
note: a segment submitted: straight to the ring's submit, or chained after the pending ones under the kernel's lock

name: D3D_SetHiZControlBit2
note: sets bit 2 (RB_HIZCONTROL) and its dirty bits

name: D3D_SetHiZControlBit3
note: sets bit 3 (RB_HIZCONTROL) and its dirty bits

name: D3D_SetHiZControlBit5
note: sets bit 5 (RB_HIZCONTROL) and its dirty bits

name: D3D_SetHiZControlByte1
note: sets bits 8-15 (RB_HIZCONTROL) and its dirty bits

name: D3D_SetSamplerForceBorderWToMax
note: sets force_bc_w_to_max (the stage's fetch constant) and its dirty bits

name: D3D_SetViewportFloats
note: the viewport as set (+12368, clamped to the surface or the tiling), its scale and offset (+10376), the scissor; dirty bits 21-26

name: D3D_SurfaceViewport
note: a surface into SURFACE_INFO and the multisample word, the runtime's scissor and viewport; dirty bits 57 and 36

name: D3D_SwapPacket
note: the swap's PM4

name: D3D_TextureDimensions
note: a texture's width, height and depth in texels from its fetch constant, by dimension

name: D3D_TextureLevelBytes
note: a texture level's sizes aligned to the format's blocks and pitch, and its bytes (4 KB rounded)

name: D3D_TileOps
note: the DPC's tile ops interpreter: each recorded segment submitted once a tile, each tile's bin select, the resources' visibility (any360/xdk/d3d_tiling.h)

name: D3D_TileSelect
note: a tile's bin select (SET_BIN_SELECT_LO) into the ring before its segments' replay (Any360: handed to the command processor)

name: D3D_UpdateShaderControl
note: the shader control bits (+10432) and the EVENT_WRITE that follows a change

name: D3D_WindowScissorPackets
note: the window scissor registers 0x2080-0x2082 (a tile at a time when tiled: bin mask, window offset, rect)

name: strcmp (loop of bytes)
note: Havok's own, inside its code in the three titles: the difference of the first bytes that differ. Any360 has xdk::CrtStrcmp for the value (checked in Test Drive Unlimited); bound in no title

name: strlen (loop of bytes)
note: Havok's own, inside its code in the three titles: middleware, kept as it is. Any360 has xdk::CrtStrlen for the value (checked in Crackdown); bound in no title

name: GetLastError
note: the thread's last error (thread + 352, the thread named by r13 + 256; 0 while r13 + 336 is not zero). Any360: xdk::XapiGetLastError, checked in the three and bound in none: five instructions, no gain as a host routine

name: SetLastError
note: stores the thread's last error (nothing while r13 + 336 is not zero). Any360: xdk::XapiSetLastError, checked in the three and bound in none: no gain as a host routine

name: XMemCpy
note: the XDK's vector copy next to XAPI: 16-byte vectors, dcbt ahead of the source, dcbz128 ahead of the destination; named after what it does (its name is not in the titles). Three builds of the same steps. Any360: xdk::XMemCpy for ranges that do not overlap, bound in the three

name: XMemSet
note: The XDK's vector fill (XMemCpy's counterpart): the low byte of r4 into r5 bytes at r3, returns r3; bytes below 16, then stvlx, 16-byte vectors stepped by a global of the title (16), 128-byte lines zeroed (dcbz128) then filled, stvrx. Named after what it does. Any360: xdk::XMemSet, bound in Crackdown (base guest, its step global at 0x82B84FE8)

name: XAudio fill 1024
note: XAudio's fill of a block's 1024 floats (from +8) with its float at +4, then 0 at +0; the same steps in the three titles. Named after what it does. Any360: xdk::XAudioFill, bound in Crackdown and Test Drive Unlimited (checked there by the self-test: its runs do not call it); not in The Simpsons Game (no run called it)

name: XAudio fill 2048
note: XAudio's fill of a block's 2048 floats (from +8) with its float at +4, then 0 at +0; the same steps in the three titles. Named after what it does. Any360: xdk::XAudioFill, bound in Crackdown and Test Drive Unlimited (checked there by the self-test: its runs do not call it); not in The Simpsons Game (no run called it)

name: XAudio fill 256
note: XAudio's fill of a block's 256 floats (from +8) with its float at +4, then 0 at +0; the same steps in the three titles. Named after what it does. name: XAudio fill 4096
note: XAudio's fill of a block's 4096 floats (from +8) with its float at +4, then 0 at +0; the same steps in the three titles. Named after what it does. Any360: xdk::XAudioFill, bound in Crackdown and Test Drive Unlimited (checked there by the self-test: its runs do not call it); not in The Simpsons Game (no run called it)

name: XAudio fill 512
note: XAudio's fill of a block's 512 floats (from +8) with its float at +4, then 0 at +0; the same steps in the three titles. Named after what it does. Any360: xdk::XAudioFill, bound in Crackdown and Test Drive Unlimited (checked there by the self-test: its runs do not call it); not in The Simpsons Game (no run called it)

name: XAudio mix ramp
note: XAudio's mix of a source into a destination with a volume ramp: four vectors of four samples at a time, vmaddfp with the gains kept in four running sums of four steps; named after what it does. Any360: xdk::XAudioMixRamp (fused, as the console and Crackdown's recompiled code), bound in Crackdown and Test Drive Unlimited (its recompiled vmaddfp is a multiply then an add, yet 269,904 mixes while driving were the same as the fused replacement's)

name: XAudio reverb
note: XAudio's I3DL2 reverb: one frame (256 samples, two channels in, four out) through ten stages (crossfading delay lines, early reflections, all-pass and comb filters, the late mix); its state in line (0x4B9D0 bytes). Any360: xdk::XAudioReverb, the function's own statements as one leaf (tools/ppc_model.py --native; hardware FMA where the build calls the C library's fma): the same bits, bound in Crackdown. The Simpsons Game has a function with the same 17,888-byte frame at 0x82C50660, likely the same (not bound: its leaf would be made from its own build)

name: png_read_filter_row
note: libpng 1.0.5's png_read_filter_row (pngrutil.c): undoes a row's filter (Sub, Up, Average, Paeth); the same instructions in Crackdown's two copies (0x82A7F5D0, the PNG loader's; 0x8280F5C8, D3DX's) and The Simpsons Game's. Any360: xdk::PngReadFilterRow (Paeth a pixel at a time in SSE2), bound in Crackdown at 0x82A7F5D0 (D3DX's copy not bound); The Simpsons Game's is D3DX's, read and not called in two scripted runs: not bound

name: zlib inflate_fast
note: zlib 1.1.4's inflate_fast (inffast.c), the decoding loop under inflate_codes: the same instructions in Crackdown's two copies (0x82A88378, under libpng 1.0.5 in the PNG loader; 0x8281BE00, the copy D3DX links) and The Simpsons Game's. Any360: xdk::InflateFast (invalid codes handed back to the function's own code), bound in Crackdown at 0x82A88378 (D3DX's copy not called on the route: not bound); The Simpsons Game's is D3DX's, read and not called in two scripted runs: not bound
